I really wanted to like this game, cute graphics, unique game mechanics that center around where to place your ingredients. However, I think the game just has a slightly too sharp difficulty curve and too high a luck-to-punishment ratio for a casual strategy game. It's very fun at lower difficulty and honestly quite addictive. Yet as the difficulty increases, runs become more and more unwinnable without saveloading, since one mistake costs you the whole run but then your run also *heavily* depends on luck with some of the NPC skills. 

I should also mention that I found the progression confusing. [spoiler] After beating the Red Apron, the subsequent Black Pantry is locked behind beating the “Final Pantry,” which I did not know how to unlock or even what it was. I had to search the Discord channel to find out that it is unlocked by “beating all pantries” or “beating all red pantries.” I had no way of verifying this myself, but if it is true, then purely from a game design perspective, it seems to me that:
[olist]
    [*] If the Final Pantry is meant to be relatively exclusive, then the Black Pantry levels should be hidden and exclusive as well. From my perspective, with unlocks in a game, you either show that there is an unlock and show how it can be unlocked, or you surprise the player by hiding both the unlock condition AND the existence of the unlock itself. Otherwise, you are leaving an element in the game that players do not know how to approach.

I normally spend hundreds of hours min/maxing these Roguelike games, but there's just something about this game that doesn't quite click for me.

I think it's the overall premise that loses me, I 'get' the gimmick of having everything on an omelette, but it's just not fun and not an enjoyable gameplay loop.

Trying to cram pieces on a tiny little board is frustrating & unsatisfying, then the end result is very nonsensical & unappealing visually. 

The hunt for another Balatro continues on...

It's actually a great game with a great style, but the current balance just makes it too frustrating. 
Being excessively RNG dependant, the shop should have by default more options. 
The run feels more about how lucky you get on the 2 or 3 first shops, than actually about strategy and reflexion,.

wait for the 67% off discount. wait for the next update. wait for more tags. realize the code make's it fun on medium and literally impossible on hard unless you do the exact line of ingredient's, buy's, sells, helper's, they want for that seed. every seed wants you to combo with things you don't have yet. don't buy this game.

It's not bad, it's jut not what i expected. There is no real depth or strategy to it, and it's quite easy, just use the good foods and don't use the obviously bad ones. Like, there's absolutely no reason to use the bad ones, despite how niche your build is.
Only real source of difficulty* comes from realtimeness of it and it's so not what roguelike deckbuilder enjoyers are looking for.

*like, it's also not hard, but the way you lose in realtime is when the hitboxes bug out (because the only real mechanic is things touching things) and suddenly you have less points than you think, and no time to hover over everything to doublecheck collision.

Some other points:
In non-realtime some things continue to be real time (burning, squid scurrying around). You already have a time resource, why not tie things to that, so there's some planning going on instead of fine motor skills. You know, "strategy".
You can just put bad ♥♥♥♥ (wrenches and so on) back on the conveyor and they just go away, i haven't seen a single reason not to or punishment for doing so.
I think when the mechanic is introduced you should get clear rules text, not "figure out how it works". You should get concrete basics and figure out combos, not the other way around.
You can still move things even if the guests quirk is that you can't. Just nudge them around with ingredient in hand.

The game is really fun WHEN it works.
Right now there is a bug which straight up bricks runs, making it unplayable, and it remains unfixed for at least a month.
Not saying to not keep an eye on this, but don't buy it just yet.

upd: The bug MIGHT be fixed now in the latest patch but I can't personally confirm it yet--the patch also has introduced several game design decisions I strongly disagree with, making playing the current "endgame" incredibly unfun. I hope and trust the devs will be able to fix some of the glaring issues in the next major update, but for now I once again can't recommend the game--it isn't what I've enjoyed playing previously.

Cool idea and theme. Very easy even on black apron with moving belts, the only thing that makes this game hard is how bad most foods are. As in I would never want to use them even if I had a niche build centered around them. Contrast to that most helpers are very powerful either just out right giving you points or disabling the negatives of the bad foods, making them at least usable or decent. I feel like there should be more interesting food combos other then +/- for touching things. On that note hitboxes are a little off, often I'll get items that overlap but don't give touch bonuses but without a current score system I don't notice til after a round.

tldr: Easy, not deep, just throw stuff on a plate and you'll do fine.

Either the calculations performed in the game are incorrect or the descriptions of abilities are. Either way, this leads to a frustrating experience when branching outside of tutorial levels and instead of opening up to more creative gameplay and complex strategies, it instead makes most of items things to avoid using thus making the game boring af

Least helpful, most confusing tutorial I've ever seen. As someone who has played a ton of Balatro/Slay the Spire-type games, I found myself not knowing what a mechanic would do, or how it might interact with other items. Not worth the frustration.

It was such an unusually cool experience but it's not really my cup of tea
First of all when you first start playing there's no tutorial, i clicked around to look and I didn't find any, the game explained in some kind of booklet what each ingredient does but it still didnt explain how you gain or lose points which meant I had to figure it out by myself which is unfair due to losing in the first few rounds and not being to get money or unlock new ingredients.
Other than that, despite it being on sale now, I still think the game should go for a cheaper sale ($3>) to be worth the price.
The graphics were great and gave this old cartoonish slightly 8-bit vibe but I don't think I'll be giving this game a try.

This one is a heavy thumbs down from me... I'm not sure how or why it is so well-rated. The start is exactly the same, at least for the first few runs, and there's only one pattern of ingredient worth making. Then, you barely have enough money for anything at the store, the synergies don't come quickly, and you get overwhelmed at like level 3 of some long series of challenges and lose. That's what happened to me four times in a row and I said... NO. Refund. It's also quite awkward to place the items and they move in a way that is frustrating at times and generally slippery/annoying when you accidentally disturb a whole cluster of your things. This is simply not fun, clearly I'm in the minority but I did not enjoy it. The aesthetics are quite nice, although turning down the "sound effects" did not turn down the sound of the voice in the tutorial so I had quite a lot of volume control issues as well.
the game is neat and the mechanics are unique, it need a bit of polish to really shine. steam really needs a middle option or a not yet option
